domain_entities.name: LeaveRequest
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee's application for leave. Tracks the full lifecycle from draft through approval/rejection to cancellation.
lifecycle_states: DRAFT — employee is composing the request; not yet visible to managers
SUBMITTED — employee has submitted; awaiting manager action
APPROVED — manager has approved; balance has been deducted
REJECTED — manager has rejected; no balance impact
CANCELLED — request was withdrawn (by employee) or cancelled after approval; if previously APPROVED, balance is restored

domain_entities.name: LeaveType
domain_entities.purpose: Enumeration of leave categories (annual, sick, emergency, unpaid, maternity, paternity). Each LeavePolicy references one LeaveType.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE — available for use in new requests and policies
INACTIVE — soft-deleted; not available for new requests but historical references remain valid

domain_entities.name: LeavePolicy
domain_entities.purpose: Defines the rules governing a specific leave type: how many days are entitled, whether manager approval is required, minimum notice period, and accrual behaviour.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE — policy is in effect; governs new leave requests
INACTIVE — policy is retired; historical requests retain their policy snapshot but new requests cannot use this policy

domain_entities.name: LeaveBalance
domain_entities.purpose: Tracks an employee's leave entitlement, consumption, and remaining balance for a specific policy within a fiscal year. Updated atomically when leave is approved or cancelled-after-approval.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE — balance is current for the fiscal year; usedDays and remainingDays are being tracked
EXHAUSTED — remainingDays has reached zero; no further leave of this type can be taken this fiscal year
CLOSED — fiscal year has ended; balance is archived and a new balance for the next fiscal year has been created

business_rules: A LeaveRequest can only be created by an employee whose employmentStatus is ACTIVE. INACTIVE or TERMINATED employees cannot submit leave. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest submission appears, not only here]

The number of leave days consumed by a request is calculated as: (endDate - startDate) + 1, i.e. both startDate and endDate are inclusive calendar days. A Monday–Friday request consumes 5 days. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest day count appears, not only here]

startDate must be on or after the current date (no backdated leave requests). endDate must be on or after startDate. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest submission appears, not only here]

When a LeaveRequest is submitted, the system must check that the employee has sufficient remainingDays in their LeaveBalance for the corresponding policy and fiscal year. The requested days must be ≤ remainingDays. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest submission appears, not only here]

Only the employee's direct manager (Employee.managerId) may approve or reject a SUBMITTED LeaveRequest. The approving actor's employeeId must match the requestor's managerId. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest approval appears, not only here]

On APPROVED transition: the employee's LeaveBalance.usedDays is incremented by the request's day count, and remainingDays is decremented by the same amount. This is an atomic operation. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest approval appears, not only here]

When an APPROVED LeaveRequest transitions to CANCELLED, the balance is restored: usedDays is decremented and remainingDays is incremented by the request's day count. Cancelling a DRAFT, SUBMITTED, or REJECTED request has no balance impact. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest cancellation appears, not only here]

If the LeavePolicy.requiresManagerApproval is false, the LeaveRequest transitions directly from DRAFT to APPROVED on submission, bypassing SUBMITTED. The balance is deducted immediately. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest submission appears, not only here]

If LeavePolicy.minimumNoticeDays is set, the gap between the submission date and startDate must be ≥ minimumNoticeDays. The gap is measured as: startDate - submissionDate, in calendar days (exclusive of submission day, inclusive of start day: startDate - submissionDate ≥ minimumNoticeDays). [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest submission appears, not only here]

An employee cannot have overlapping APPROVED or SUBMITTED LeaveRequests for the same date range. Overlap is defined as: existing.startDate ≤ new.endDate AND existing.endDate ≥ new.startDate. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest submission appears, not only here]

When remainingDays reaches 0, the LeaveBalance transitions from ACTIVE to EXHAUSTED. No further leave of that type can be approved for that fiscal year. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveBalance lifecycle appears, not only here]

Valid state transitions: DRAFT→SUBMITTED, DRAFT→CANCELLED, SUBMITTED→APPROVED, SUBMITTED→REJECTED, SUBMITTED→CANCELLED, APPROVED→CANCELLED. REJECTED and CANCELLED are terminal states (no further transitions). [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest state transitions appears, not only here]

Emergency leave bypasses the minimumNoticeDays check. The LeavePolicy for emergency leave may set minimumNoticeDays to null or 0, but even if set, the emergency nature overrides it. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest submission appears, not only here]

If LeavePolicy.accrualRate is set (non-null, > 0), the LeaveBalance.totalEntitlement is not a fixed annual grant but grows over the fiscal year at the specified rate (e.g. 1.25 days/month). The accrued amount must not exceed LeavePolicy.maxAccumulation if set. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveBalance accrual appears, not only here]

An employee may cancel their own LeaveRequest in DRAFT or SUBMITTED state. Only a manager (or HR admin) may cancel an APPROVED LeaveRequest. A REJECTED or already-CANCELLED request cannot be cancelled again. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest cancellation appears, not only here]
domain_notes:
## Lifecycle states introduced

- **LeaveRequest**: DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED — with explicit transition map: DRAFT→SUBMITTED, DRAFT→CANCELLED, SUBMITTED→APPROVED, SUBMITTED→REJECTED, SUBMITTED→CANCELLED, APPROVED→CANCELLED. REJECTED and CANCELLED are terminal.
- **LeaveType**: ACTIVE, INACTIVE — controls availability for new requests/policies.
- **LeavePolicy**: ACTIVE, INACTIVE — governs whether the policy applies to new requests.
- **LeaveBalance**: ACTIVE, EXHAUSTED, CLOSED — tracks fiscal-year lifecycle; EXHAUSTED when remainingDays=0; CLOSED at fiscal year end.

## Cross-entity concerns

- **Audit**: Every state-changing operation on LeaveRequest (submit, approve, reject, cancel) and LeaveBalance (deduction, restoration) must produce an AuditRecord per GP-002.
- **Notification**: LeaveRequest state transitions trigger notifications: SUBMITTED → notify manager; APPROVED/REJECTED → notify employee; CANCELLED → notify the other party.
- **Employee**: Leave operations depend on Employee.employmentStatus (must be ACTIVE), Employee.managerId (for approval routing), and Employee.hireDate (may affect eligibility).
- **LeavePolicy ↔ LeaveBalance**: Each LeaveBalance is scoped to one LeavePolicy; the policy's entitlementDays, accrualRate, and maxAccumulation govern the balance's totalEntitlement and accrual behaviour.
- **LeavePolicy ↔ LeaveRequest**: Policy rules (requiresManagerApproval, minimumNoticeDays) control request validation and auto-approval paths.

## Open design decisions for chief architect

1. Calendar days vs working days for leave counting (currently assumed inclusive calendar days).
2. Fiscal year boundary definition (currently unset — needed for balance lifecycle).
3. Emergency leave auto-approval behaviour (currently emergency bypasses minimumNoticeDays but manager-approval question is open).

open_questions.question: Should leave day counting use calendar days (inclusive: endDate - startDate + 1) or working/business days (excluding weekends and/or public holidays)?
open_questions.impact: Affects balance deduction, sufficiency checks, policy minimum/maximum validations, and reporting. The current domain rule assumes inclusive calendar days, but many organisations count only working days for annual leave while using calendar days for sick leave.
candidate_options: Calendar days (inclusive) — simplest, uniform across all leave types
Working days (exclude weekends) — common for annual leave in many jurisdictions
Per-policy configurable — each LeavePolicy specifies its own counting method
Working days excluding public holidays — requires a holiday calendar integration

open_questions.question: What is the fiscal year boundary? (e.g. calendar year Jan 1–Dec 31, or April 6–April 5 for UK tax year, or company-specific)
open_questions.impact: Determines when LeaveBalance transitions from ACTIVE/EXHAUSTED to CLOSED, when new balances are created, and how carry-over/accrual rules apply. Affects the balance lifecycle and the fiscalYear field assignment.
candidate_options: Fixed to a specific jurisdiction (e.g. UK: April 6 – April 5)

open_questions.question: Should emergency leave bypass the manager-approval requirement even when the policy says requiresManagerApproval=true? Or should it always require approval but with a shorter SLA?
open_questions.impact: Affects the auto-approval path for emergency leave. If emergency leave auto-approves, balance is deducted immediately without manager review, which has compliance implications.
candidate_options: Emergency leave always requires manager approval (policy controls it)
Emergency leave auto-approves regardless of policy setting
Emergency leave has a separate policy flag (e.g. emergencyAutoApproves)
